<p class="section-label">Research Practice</p>

# Methods

I choose methods based on the question. Most of my projects pair computational analysis of large text collections with close qualitative reading, and some add statistical modeling, experiments, or spatial analysis.

## Computational text analysis

I use computational framing analysis to study how corporate AI governance documents justify their commitments and assign responsibility. For news coverage at scale, I work with dictionary methods, named entity recognition, sentiment scaling, and clustering. In R, I have built the full pipeline from cleaning raw text to building corpora, applying psycholinguistic norms, and comparing word embeddings with human ratings of meaning.

[NLP in R course portfolio](https://ahmypeace.github.io/CSD5730_NLP_R_Spring2026/){target="_blank"}

## Qualitative and interpretive methods

My master's thesis drew on in-depth interviews with 18 Nigerian news workers, analyzed through thematic analysis. I also use discourse and framing analysis to read policy documents, news stories, and corporate texts closely, often alongside a computational pass over the same material.

## Statistical modeling and experiments

I use statistical modeling to test predictors of attitudes and behavior, including a study of the cognitive, behavioral, and emotional predictors of perceived control over personal data. Newer work uses computational experiments and AI evaluation, including synthetic users and persona-based evaluators, to test how stable machine judgments are.

## Spatial analysis

I use GIS to map social and environmental problems. Recent work in ArcGIS Pro screened Flint for drinking-water risk, located Los Angeles schools near methane-producing landfills, and searched for a site for a healthy food store in Philadelphia.

[GIS lab portfolio](https://ahmypeace.github.io/gis-lab-report/){target="_blank"}

## Tools

- **Python:** pandas, spaCy, scikit-learn, Jupyter
- **R:** quanteda, tidyverse, ggplot2, textstem, R Markdown
- **Mapping:** ArcGIS Pro and the ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript
- **Workflow:** Git, GitHub, and Quarto

## Tools I have built

[Chota](https://ahmypeace.github.io/Chota/){target="_blank"} is a browser app for manual content analysis. Coders read each article PDF and code it on the same screen, then export the data to SPSS, Excel, CSV, R, or Python. I built it to code news coverage for my own studies, and the [source is on GitHub](https://github.com/ahmypeace/Chota){target="_blank"}.
